## 1. Overview

*Introduction to Industrial and Manufacturing Systems Engineering* is a first-year textbook for IMSE 111 (3 credits) at North Dakota State University. It does two jobs that existing books usually split between separate texts. It introduces the **profession**: what IMEs do, where they work, and how they think about systems of people, materials, information, equipment, and energy [@iise-definition]. It also builds the **toolkit** that first-year students need: spreadsheets and Python for data, project planning, technical writing, and presentations.

The book grows out of the IMSE 111 lecture notes at North Dakota State University, which follow the NDSU catalog description of the course [@ndsu-catalog-ime]. It is written and published with Quarto, so the same source produces an accessible website and a print-ready manuscript.

## 2. Need and rationale

**[TO DO: expand from teaching experience.]** Starting points:

- First-year students often pick a major before they know what industrial engineering is. A readable introduction built on real stories helps recruit and keep students.
- Most introductory IE texts are either broad surveys with few hands-on computational exercises, or tool manuals with little connection to the profession.
- Employers expect graduates to be comfortable with data. Introducing Python through browser-based notebooks (Google Colab) removes the installation barrier in the first semester.

## 3. Audience and market

- **Primary:** first-year students in introduction to industrial, manufacturing, or systems engineering courses.
- **Secondary:** general introduction to engineering courses, community college pre-engineering programs, and professionals moving into operations roles.
- **Course fit:** one semester, 15 weeks, one chapter per week.

**[TO DO: add enrollment figures for IMSE 111 and comparable courses.]**

## 4. Distinctive features

| Feature | What it gives students |
|:--|:--|
| Highlighted IE vocabulary | Key terms are marked in the text, defined on hover in the web edition, and collected in a glossary and per-chapter key-term lists. |
| Stories from the field | Short, sourced stories (for example, Lillian Gilbreth's kitchen) that tie concepts to people and places. |
| Colab notebooks | One runnable Python notebook per chapter. No installation needed. |
| In-class activities and career spotlights | Ready-to-use exercises for active learning, plus profiles of real roles. |
| Open web edition and print manuscript | One Quarto source produces both. The web edition is searchable, mobile-friendly, and supports dark mode. |

## 5. Competing and complementary titles

| Title | Strength | How this book differs |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Turner, Mize, Case & Nazemetz, *Introduction to Industrial and Systems Engineering* [@turner1993] | Classic survey of IE | Current examples, computational notebooks, careers focus |
| Groover, *Fundamentals of Modern Manufacturing* [@groover2019] | Comprehensive manufacturing processes | First-year level; systems and careers rather than process depth |
| Freivalds & Niebel, *Niebel's Methods, Standards, and Work Design* [@freivalds2013] | Authoritative on work design | Covers work design as one chapter in a broad introduction |
| Hopp & Spearman, *Factory Physics* [@hopp2008] | Rigorous operations science | Intuitive first exposure to the same ideas (bottlenecks, Little's Law) |

**[TO DO: add any recent introductory titles the publisher suggests.]**

13. Planning and Managing Engineering Projects
14. Technical Reports and Professional Presentations
15. Ethics, Sustainability, and the Future of IME

**Appendices:** Colab Notebooks · Glossary · References
